acceptanceCriteria: Spike decides whether this belongs in Corvint hosts or is left to the host, recording the decision in docs/build-log with the invariant 4, 5 and 7 analysis.
If pursued: a spec defines the event classes, the byte bound, secret screening and the restore digest, and states that the ledger is never an input to ranking, evidence or authority.
Evaluation compares post-compaction task continuation with and without the restored digest on a frozen task set; missing telemetry stays NOT_OBSERVED.
body: Source: GitHub trending review 2026-10-16 (idea only; nothing was adopted or measured). Prior art: mksglu/context-mode captures structured events through PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hooks (file edits, user corrections, tool calls the user denied, error then fix sequences, blockers, environment changes), snapshots them at PreCompact, and restores a bounded digest at SessionStart. Corvint today re-pins authority at compaction (V1-0094, kernel/CKN-V0) and plans ticket-level resume context (V1-0472) and checkpoint handoff qualification (V1-0473), but nothing retains the session's own working state, such as rejected approaches and user corrections, across compaction. Constraints: invariant 4 (reads do not mutate; any new ledger needs its own bounded private writer spec in the SOL-V0 family and must never feed ranking, evidence or authority); invariant 5 (secret screening before retention); invariant 7 (no database service; context-mode uses SQLite FTS5, so Corvint would need an append-only bounded file). Overlap check: V1-0472, V1-0473, V1-0094 cover adjacent but distinct scope.
title: Idea: hook-captured session working state that survives compaction (decisions, rejected approaches, error-to-fix pairs)
